newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerians want foreign oil monitors sent packing.
newsitem.headline: Nigerians want foreign oil monitors sent packing.

text.p: Staff of the Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR), which supervises Nigerian oil exports, have begun a campaign for the authorities to do away with foreign oil monitors, their leaders said on Tuesday.
Leaders of the DPR chapters of the oil workers unions NUPENG and PENGASSAN said the monitors were irrelevant and a waste of scarce national resources.
"DPR workers are still the ones doing the visualisation and documentation of oil lifting at the terminals," one of the union leaders told the official Daily Times newspaper.
The two foreign monitors, Global Inspection Services and Robinson International, were appointed last April to vet the quantity of crude oil exports at the terminals.

Their appointment followed allegations that Nigeria was losing revenue because some DPR staff were colluding with foreign lifters to cheat through a system of "topping", loading more crude than was declared on paper, and pocketing the proceeds.
DPR staff vehemently opposed the appointment at the time.
Daily Times said the union leaders argued that almost a year after the monitors started work there had been no report of illegal oil lifting and therefore they should be withdrawn.
Apart from usurping the functions of issuing final certificates of quality and quantity of crude lifted, the continued stay of the monitors was a drain on the nation's resources, they added.
DPR staff who had not been paid since January were scheduled to go on strike from Friday but called off the action after the government raised money to pay their January salaries and rent subsidies.
Their monthly wage bill is 32 million naira or $400,000, a fraction of the $15 million annual fees of the monitors.
